title: Janitor 'Silent Patchlet' and Support Telemetry Adaptor
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a small, idempotent admin utility ('Silent Patchlet') that operators can run as a single task from the Console/CLI to apply low-risk, reversible fixes for common support scenarios (eg. ephemeral worker restart, routing tag tweak, KV cache prime). The Patchlet will be modeled as a runbook-as-task primitive (templated inputs, dry-run mode, automatic rollback hooks) and will emit structured telemetry via a dedicated adaptor so each execution is auditable, traceable, and linkable to an alert or ticket. Goals: 1) reduce mean time to mitigation for recurring low-risk incidents; 2) make operator actions replayable and safe; 3) ensure each action leaves enough telemetry to correlate with latency/cost regressions in dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A CLI/Console UI can launch a 'silent-patch' task with parameters and dry-run option
Patchlet actions are idempotent or have a verified rollback path
Each execution generates a structured telemetry event (schema v1) stored in ops-events with fields: operator, task_key, inputs_hash, result, start_ts, end_ts, rollback_performed
Runbook-as-task template stored in runbooks library and discoverable from Console search
Integration test that simulates a common incident (stuck worker) and verifies automatic rollback when a safety check fails
Security/permissions: only roles with ops:execute and ops:patchlet privileges can run; audit log entries created
Documentation PR (Confluence) and quickstart in Console for SREs and Oncall
tasks: Spike: list target fix actions and define safe default timeouts
Design: telemetry event schema and retention/PII review
Implementation: lightweight Go CLI wrapper + Console button route
Server: create /admin/patchlet-run endpoint with idempotency key handling
Safety: implement preflight checks and automatic rollback hooks
QA: create smoke harness and chaos scenario for rollback verification
Docs: Confluence runbook + Console quickstart + playbook snippet
